title: DiffServe: Efficiently Serving Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Query-Aware Model Scaling
problem: Text-to-image diffusion model serving faces two simultaneous challenges: high-quality models (e.g., SDv1.5 at 50 steps) are 4.6-18x slower than lightweight variants (SD-Turbo, SDXS), limiting throughput; and query demand fluctuates, causing static resource provisioning to either waste capacity during off-peak or fail SLOs during peak.
motivation: For 20-40% of queries, lightweight diffusion models produce images of equal or better quality than heavyweight models ('easy queries'). Routing these queries to lightweight models saves compute. However, existing metrics (CLIP Score, PickScore) cannot reliably identify easy queries (they perform no better than random routing), so a task-specific discriminator is needed. Dynamic resource allocation must co-optimize discriminator confidence threshold, model variant placement, and batch sizes.
method: DiffServe routes requests through a lightweight model first, then uses a classifier (EfficientNet-V2) to decide if the result is good enough or should be redone by the heavyweight model; the classifier was trained on real photographs (MSCOCO) and generated images, with the counterintuitive finding that training with only real photos as 'good' works better than also using heavyweight outputs. A controller periodically solves an optimization equation (Mixed Integer Linear Program) that adjusts device counts, batch sizes, and the classifier's confidence threshold to meet latency and throughput targets as demand fluctuates (tracked via exponential smoothing with 5% safety margin), solving asynchronously in ~10ms outside the serving path.
key_novelty: DiffServe combines a real-or-fake image classifier (EfficientNet-V2) trained on real photographs versus generated images to intelligently route queries between lightweight and heavyweight diffusion models, paired with an optimization algorithm that jointly adjusts confidence thresholds, batch sizes, and device allocation to meet quality and throughput targets under changing demand.
contributions: Query-aware model cascade for text-to-image diffusion serving using a trained discriminator
EfficientNet-V2 discriminator trained on real images outperforms PickScore/ClipScore/random for query routing
MILP resource allocation co-optimizing confidence threshold, batch sizes, and device counts
Demonstration that routing 20-40% of queries to lightweight models improves system FID (quality) vs all-heavyweight
Simulator (7K Python lines) + 16 A100 testbed evaluation with 0.56% FID discrepancy

metrics.quality_vs_proteus: Up to 20% FID improvement vs Proteus (random query-agnostic routing)
metrics.quality_vs_static: Up to 24% FID improvement vs static configurations
metrics.slo_violations_vs_static: 19-70% lower SLO violation rate vs static provisioning
metrics.slo_violations_vs_clipper_heavy: Up to 52x lower SLO violation vs Clipper-Heavy

baselines: Proteus (dynamic model selection, random query routing)
limitations: Discriminator training requires curating real/fake image datasets and offline model profiling
MILP assumes deterministic execution times; variance in GPU execution affects queuing model accuracy
Cascade depth limited to two models; extending to multi-stage cascades requires more complex MILP
Reusing intermediate lightweight outputs in heavyweight inference showed mixed results (quality sometimes degraded)
